title: Terraform module gated upgrades for VPC control-plane: compatibility checks and canary roll forward
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a Terraform-first gated upgrade flow for private (VPC) control-plane upgrades. The goal is to ensure we can apply control-plane version changes using dedicated Terraform modules that perform preflight compatibility checks, run a lightweight canary promotion (tfplan applied to a canary VPC), and automatically validate runtime health and API compatibility before rolling changes to customer VPCs.

Why: Current upgrade automation relies on ad-hoc orchestration and staged scripts that make it hard to reproducibly validate IaC changes. By encoding gates and compatibility checks in Terraform modules and CI pipelines we reduce human error, improve reproducibility, and make rollbacks deterministic.

Scope:
- Add schema compatibility validations to our control-plane Terraform modules (module inputs/outputs, CRD/operator version compatibility).
- Build an automated "tfplan-runner" job in the infra CI that: (1) runs plan against a canary VPC compute stack, (2) applies the canary, (3) triggers synthetic validation suite, (4) conditionally promotes changes.
- Implement runtime health checks (API smoke tests, control-plane leader election sanity, certificate expiry check, operator reconciliation latency, core RPC p95) and wire results into the Console rollout dashboard.
- Implement automatic state-safe rollback path and operator/pod image pinning for canary to stable promotion steps.

Out of scope:
- Large-scale data migrations of customer workloads (handled separately).
- Non-Terraform upgrade pathways (helm-only flows).

Design notes:
- Compatibility checks will be a mix of static and dynamic checks: static (schema diffs, provider version constraints, immutable field diffs) are executed at plan-time; dynamic checks (CRD compatibility smoke, operator reconciliation) run after canary apply.
- Canary VPC will be isolated with minimal test-tenants; traffic will be shadowed from production paths where safe. The canary run is NOT intended to run full traffic for every upgrade — only minimal API surface and stateful scenarios needed to validate control-plane behavior.
- The Terraform modules will expose a gating flag (module.upgrade_gate.policy) with options: MANUAL, AUTOMATIC, STAGED. The CI will respect this policy when deciding whether to auto-promote.
- State management: use remote state with strict locks and a preflight state snapshot (terraform state pull saved to artifact) to enable deterministic rollback.

Risks / trade-offs:
- More complexity in Terraform modules increases maintenance cost. To mitigate, keep gating logic thin and implement heavy checks in the CI runner (external scripts) rather than in HCL.
- Canary false negatives when canary VPC doesn't capture all customer topologies. We'll mitigate by running periodic topological smoke matrices against representative host patterns.

Next steps:
1) Draft Terraform module changes and provider pinning RFC (this ticket).
2) Prototype tfplan-runner in the infra CI sandbox (2-week spike).
3) Implement health check suite and Console dashboard wiring (parallel).
4) Run a small internal canary with engineering-only VPCs, iterate on failure modes.

Deliverables: terraform module PR, CI job, synthetic test suite, Console rollout gating integration, runbook for rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform control-plane modules expose a compatibility check hook and an upgrade_gate.policy option
CI tfplan-runner can run plan/apply to an isolated canary VPC and emit pass/fail status
Synthetic health checks (API smoke, operator reconciliation latency, leader-election status) run automatically post-canary apply and report to Console
Automated rollback artifact saved (state snapshot and pinned image list) for failed canary runs
Documentation + runbook exist describing manual override and emergency rollback steps
